tool_arguments.query: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers fiscal 2025

events.content: NVIDIA Data Center revenue growth drivers fiscal 2025

**NVIDIA’s Data Center revenue reached $115.2 billion in FY2025** (year ended January 26, 2025), a **142% year-over-year increase** from $47.5 billion in FY2024; it was the central source of the company’s 114% total-revenue growth. [[1]] [[2]]

**Primary growth drivers**

- **Hopper accelerated-computing demand was the dominant driver.** NVIDIA said Data Center computing revenue grew **162%** year over year, principally due to Hopper-platform demand for large-language models, recommendation engines, and generative-AI applications. [[3]]
- **AI model scaling increased infrastructure requirements.** NVIDIA attributed rising Data Center-system demand to advances in accelerated computing and generative-AI models, as well as increasing model complexity and scale. [[3]]
- **Cloud-provider and enterprise AI build-outs supported volume.** NVIDIA’s products were being deployed through major cloud platforms—including AWS, CoreWeave, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud—to meet customer AI demand, underpinning broad-based capacity expansion. [[1]]
- **Networking was a meaningful secondary contributor.** Data Center networking revenue increased **51%** year over year, driven by Ethernet-for-AI revenue, including NVIDIA’s Spectrum-X end-to-end Ethernet platform. [[3]]
- **Blackwell began contributing late in the year.** NVIDIA started shipping production Blackwell systems in FY2025’s fourth quarter and reported billions of dollars of Blackwell AI-supercomputer sales in that initial production quarter, adding a new growth leg while Hopper remained the full-year engine. [[3]] [[4]]
- **The revenue ramp accelerated through the year.** Quarterly Data Center revenue rose from **$22.6 billion in Q1** to **$26.3 billion in Q2**, **$30.8 billion in Q3**, and **$35.6 billion in Q4**, reflecting sustained Hopper demand, continuing AI-infrastructure deployment, and the initial Blackwell ramp. [[5]] [[6]] [[7]] [[1]]

**Mix perspective:** Data Center compute generated **$102.2 billion** of FY2025 revenue, versus $39.0 billion in FY2024, and therefore accounted for the overwhelming majority of the platform’s $67.7 billion absolute revenue increase; networking supplied the remainder of the growth. [[2]] [[3]]

**Bottom line:** FY2025 Data Center growth was chiefly an AI-compute capacity cycle—hyperscalers, model builders, and enterprises buying Hopper-based systems for training and inference—with Spectrum-X networking expansion and the late-year Blackwell production ramp  …[truncated]
